alternatives_considered: Full RFP to alternate RCM vendors (e.g., eClinicalWorks, NextGen) if targets not met
battlecards.why_selected: Reduced fee tier to 3.15% while avoiding $9 M early-termination liability and preserving integrated EHR/PM platform.
battlecards.contract_terms: Addendum effective 9/1/22; 3.15 % of collections through Jan-2025; pricing applied retroactively to 9/1/22.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Market benchmarks showed Advantia 40-60 bps above peers; threatened RFP or migration to athenaCollector; upcoming growth gave volume leverage.
supplier_strengths: High user adoption and embedded workflows
battlecards.switching_costs: ≈ $9 M early-termination fee plus system migration and retraining.
battlecards.notes: Addendum under legal review at time of project close-out.

battlecards.why_selected: Lowest total-cost offer, committed implementation team, and agreed to 60-day terms; strong formulary & reporting tools.
battlecards.contract_terms: 3-year master distribution agreement with two 1-year renewal options; quarterly business reviews; 60-day payment terms; price-cap clauses.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Aggregated volume across Heartland & Mid-Atlantic, multi-round RFP with target-price feedback.
supplier_strengths: Broad product breadth and nationwide DC network
supplier_weaknesses: Higher minimum order quantities than Medline
battlecards.switching_costs: Formulary cross-walk, EDI set-up, staff training on McKesson ordering portal.
battlecards.notes: Heartland sites move from Medline to McKesson; Mid-Atlantic remains distributor-neutral but under McKesson contract pricing.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pricing was 8-10 % above McKesson’s BAFO and could not match 60-day payment terms or enterprise reporting requirements.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat of losing all Heartland volume forced Medline to sharpen pricing but still fell short.
battlecards.switching_costs: Minor ― product crosswalk and ordering portal change already handled during McKesson implementation.
battlecards.notes: Remains a back-up supplier for unforeseen shortages only.

battlecards.why_selected: Met 10 % savings target while avoiding operational change; maintains embedded phlebotomists and LIS interfaces.
battlecards.contract_terms: Revised pricing locked until Oct-2024; 90-day out clause; surcharge cap on top 50 tests.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Quest BAFO showed 16 % savings—used as credible switch threat.
battlecards.switching_costs: Rebuilding interfaces, re-training staff, and potential patient disruption.
battlecards.notes: Savings begin 11/1/22, contingent on contract addendum execution.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Higher savings offset by operational risk of switching labs across 24 sites; decision made to remain with incumbent.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Provided lowest BAFO pricing that forced LabCorp concessions.
supplier_weaknesses: No embedded staff at Advantia sites
battlecards.switching_costs: LIS build, courier route changes, phlebotomist staffing.
battlecards.notes: Kept as future alternative for next bid cycle.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Pay-per-scan pricing 20 % above market; unresponsive to negotiation outreach; insourcing delivered best long-term economics.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Threat to exit contract and hire sonographers directly.
battlecards.notes: Final IT Imaging invoices paid through Aug-2022 before transition.

battlecards.why_selected: Provides flexible recruiting support for ~20 % of demand at rates 22–24 % below incumbent cost.
battlecards.contract_terms: Month-to-month SOW; bill rate $94–118 K per FTE sourced; 30-day termination.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Volume forecast and commitment to 20 % utilization secured lower bill rates.
supplier_weaknesses: Not a full turn-key staffing firm
battlecards.notes: Supplements in-house recruiter; budget assumes 20 % utilization.

battlecards.why_selected: USWHA contract already delivered deep discounts; policy change captured missed tier discounts and program enrollment added replacement credits.
battlecards.contract_terms: USWHA agreement through 12/31/2022; discounts tiered by 5-unit order minimums.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Data showed 0 % discount orders; enforcing MOQ recovered lost discounts.
supplier_weaknesses: MOQ compliance required to realize savings
battlecards.switching_costs: Low product switching cost but clinical preference for Mirena/Kyleena drove decision.
battlecards.notes: Additional $21.6 K annual value from Confidence in Coverage program (separate line item).
complexity_reasons: Program enrollment and MOQ enforcement needed

summary.skipped_reason: Other suppliers were simple renewals, data-only vendors, or categories still in progress (e.g., IT Managed Services).
